trial_name.text: Study CS2 (ISIS 420915-CS2), the single adequate and well-controlled pivotal trial

citations.quote: A single clinical trial, Study CS2, was intended to provide substantial evidence of the effectiveness of inotersen for the treatment of the polyneuropathy associated with hATTR in adults.

Study CS2 was a 66-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in adult patients with polyneuropathy caused by hATTR.

design.text: 66-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial conducted at 24 sites in 10 countries; patients randomized 2:1 to inotersen 284 mg SC weekly (recommended dosage per label; the review describes it on the salt basis as 300 mg doses following 3 loading doses in Week 1) or placebo.

population.text: Adults 18-82 years with hATTR amyloidosis with a documented TTR gene mutation and biopsy-documented amyloid deposition, Stage 1 or Stage 2 polyneuropathy, and baseline NIS of 10 to 130.

citations.quote: Patients were required to be between 18 to 82 years of age, have a diagnosis of hATTR amyloidosis with a documented mutation in the TTR gene, and have documented amyloid deposition assessed by biopsy. Patients were also required to have Stage 1 or Stage 2 polyneuropathy and have a baseline Neuropathy Impairment Score (NIS) score of 10 to 130 (higher scores indicate more severe polyneuropathy). result.text: Both co-primary endpoints significantly favored inotersen at Week 66: mNIS+7 LS mean treatment difference -19.7 [95% CI -26.4, -13.0], p<0.001; Norfolk QoL-DN LS mean treatment difference -11.7 [95% CI -18.3, -5.1], p<0.001.

indication.text: TEGSEDI is indicated for the treatment of the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults.

citations.quote: TEGSEDI is indicated for the treatment of the polyneuropathy of hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis in adults.

target_moa.text: Inotersen is a 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl) phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide that selectively binds to TTR mRNA, causing degeneration of both wild-type and mutant TTR mRNA and reducing serum TTR protein by an average of 70%.

citations.quote: Inotersen is a 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl) [2' MOE] phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) that selectively binds to TTR messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) causing degeneration of both wild-type and mutant TTR mRNA. The dose of inotersen that is proposed for marketing has been demonstrated to reduce serum TTR protein levels by an average of 70%.
Inotersen is a 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl) [2' MOE] phosphorothioate ASO inhibitor of both mutant and wild type human TTR production.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥20% and more frequent than placebo) were injection site reactions, nausea, headache, fatigue, thrombocytopenia, and fever. Injection site reactions 49% vs 10%, nausea 31% vs 12%, thrombocytopenia 24% vs 2%. Serious risks include severe thrombocytopenia (platelet counts <100 x10^9/L in 25% vs 2%) and glomerulonephritis (occurred in 3% of TEGSEDI-treated patients vs no patient on placebo).

TEGSEDI can cause glomerulonephritis that may result in dialysis-dependent renal failure. In Study 1 [see *Clinical studies* (14)], glomerulonephritis occurred in three (3%) TEGSEDI-treated patients vs. no patient on placebo.

detail.text: Boxed warning for Thrombocytopenia and Glomerulonephritis: TEGSEDI causes reductions in platelet count that may result in sudden, unpredictable, life-threatening thrombocytopenia (one trial patient died from intracranial hemorrhage); it can cause glomerulonephritis that may require immunosuppressive treatment and may result in dialysis-dependent renal failure. Both require prior testing and monitoring during treatment.

citations.quote: TEGSEDI causes reductions in platelet count that may result in sudden and unpredictable thrombocytopenia, which can be life-threatening. One clinical trial patient died from intracranial hemorrhage.

detail.text: TEGSEDI is available only through a restricted distribution program under a REMS (the TEGSEDI REMS Program) because of risks of serious bleeding caused by severe thrombocytopenia and because of glomerulonephritis, both of which require frequent monitoring.

citations.quote: Because of the risks of serious bleeding caused by severe thrombocytopenia and because of glomerulonephritis, both of which require frequent monitoring, TEGSEDI is available only through a restricted distribution program under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) called the TEGSEDI REMS Program [see *Warnings and Precautions* (5.3)].

vote.text: This application was not referred to an advisory committee because the clinical trial design was acceptable, the efficacy findings were clear, and the safety profile was acceptable for the lethal disease being treated.

citations.quote: This application was not referred for review to an advisory committee because the clinical trial design is acceptable, and the efficacy findings were clear, and the safety profile, despite the considerable serious toxicity, was acceptable for the lethal disease being treated.
